CHIEF COMPLAINT
Incidentally found right upper lobe lung nodule.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents for evaluation of a lung nodule discovered during imaging workup for cough. Patient reports approximately 3 months of intermittent cough that began after loading hay while working with horses, followed by development of cold. Primary care physician diagnosed bronchitis and obtained chest X-ray to exclude pneumonia, which revealed the lung nodule. Subsequent CT scan confirmed the finding and patient was referred for pulmonary evaluation. Cough has since resolved. Patient maintains an active lifestyle with regular biking and reports he does not typically get sick.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or dyspnea. Denies fever. Good exercise tolerance.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis, well-controlled. History of tobacco use, quit approximately 7 years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly for rheumatoid arthritis.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with history of breast cancer, currently doing well. Denies family history of lung cancer, other malignancies, lung infections, or pneumonia.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Occupational: Works with horses. Active lifestyle with regular biking, prefers trail riding. Former smoker, quit 7 years ago, denies current tobacco use.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: BP 124/76, HR 70, RR 16, O2 saturation 98% on room air, afebrile. Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs, rubs, or clicks; no ectopy. Extremities: Skin pink, warm, dry; no lower extremity edema; mild swelling of knuckles on third digits bilaterally consistent with rheumatoid arthritis; pulses intact all extremities; capillary refill brisk.

RESULTS
Chest CT: Solitary 2 cm smooth nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe. No evidence of emphysematous disease.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right upper lobe lung nodule: Order pulmonary function tests for baseline lung function assessment. Schedule PET CT to determine if nodule is metabolically active. Plan video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery for nodule removal with small portion of adjacent lung tissue under general anesthesia (approximately 1.5 hours duration). Post-operative admission overnight with chest tube placement, anticipated discharge post-operative day 1. Patient counseled regarding procedure risks, benefits, and alternatives.

Rheumatoid arthritis: Continue follow-up with rheumatologist and continue methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly as previously prescribed.

Patient expressed anxiety; reassured regarding close follow-up and support throughout treatment. Paperwork to follow.
